title: Integrate Overpass API real-time hospital detection with routing into ResourceMapPage and HospitalFinderPage

requirements.summary: Rewrite ResourceMapPage to fetch real nearby hospitals from Overpass API, merge with backend hospitals, and display only those within 5 km sorted by distance
acceptanceCriteria: On page mount, geolocation is requested automatically.
Overpass API is queried with the user's real GPS coordinates and a radius of 10 km.
Only hospitals within 5 km are shown as Leaflet markers and in the sidebar.
Hospitals are sorted by distance, nearest first.
If no hospitals are within 5 km, the sidebar displays 'No hospitals found within 5 km' and no markers appear.
Backend-registered hospitals are merged with Overpass results (deduplication by proximity or name).
Loading and error states are displayed correctly.

file_operations.description: Rewrite the component to fetch hospitals from both the backend (via useGetHospitals) and the Overpass API (https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter) using the user's live GPS coordinates from useGeolocation. Query Overpass for nodes with amenity=hospital or healthcare=hospital within a 10 km radius. Parse the Overpass JSON response, compute haversine distances from the user to each hospital, merge backend and Overpass results (deduplicating by proximity or name match), filter to only include hospitals within 5 km, and sort by distance nearest-first. Update the Leaflet map markers and sidebar list to display only the filtered and sorted hospitals. Show 'No hospitals found within 5 km' in the sidebar if no results are within range. Handle loading states while waiting for geolocation and API responses, and display error messages if geolocation is denied or the API call fails.

Create a utility module that exports functions for querying the Overpass API. Include a function buildOverpassQuery(lat, lng, radiusKm) that constructs the Overpass QL query string for amenity=hospital or healthcare=hospital within the specified radius, and a function fetchNearbyHospitals(lat, lng, radiusKm) that posts the query to https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter and returns a typed array of hospital results parsed from the Overpass JSON response (extracting name, lat, lng, and relevant tags). Add error handling for network failures and empty result sets.

requirements.summary: Integrate leaflet-routing-machine for in-map turn-by-turn directions on ResourceMapPage, with OSRM routing and styled route lines
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking 'Get Directions' on a popup or sidebar item draws a route line from user location to the hospital.
The OSRM router (https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1) is used for routing.
The route line uses the app accent color (red/amber).
A 'Close Directions' button removes the active routing control.
No duplicate routing controls are added — the previous one is removed before adding a new one.
If geolocation is not available, the 'Get Directions' button is disabled with tooltip 'Enable location to get directions'.

file_operations.description: Add state to track the active routing control instance. Add 'Get Directions' buttons to both the hospital marker popups and the sidebar list items. When a button is clicked, remove any existing routing control from the map, then create a new L.Routing.control with waypoints from the user's current coordinates (from useGeolocation) to the selected hospital's lat/lng, using the OSRM router at https://router.project-osrm.org/route/v1. Style the route line with the app accent color (#ef4444 or similar red/amber). Add a 'Close Directions' button in the UI that removes the routing control when clicked. Disable the 'Get Directions' button with a tooltip 'Enable location to get directions' if geolocation is unavailable or still loading.
Add leaflet-routing-machine and its TypeScript type definitions (@types/leaflet-routing-machine) to the dependencies to support turn-by-turn routing on the map.

requirements.summary: Update HospitalFinderPage to fetch hospitals from both backend and Overpass API, merge results, and display with distance and extracted address/phone
acceptanceCriteria: HospitalFinderPage fetches hospitals from both the backend and the Overpass API.
Overpass results include address parsed from addr:street, addr:city, addr:housenumber tags.
Overpass results include phone from phone or contact:phone tags where available.
Distance from user location is calculated for all results using the haversine utility.
Existing distance and availability filters apply to the merged list.
The page is styled with the existing CrisisConnect emergency dark theme.

file_operations.description: Update the component to fetch hospitals from both the backend (via useGetHospitals) and the Overpass API (using the fetchNearbyHospitals utility with the user's GPS coordinates from useGeolocation). Parse address from Overpass tags (addr:housenumber, addr:street, addr:city, addr:postcode) and phone from tags (phone, contact:phone). Compute distances for all hospitals using the haversine utility. Merge backend and Overpass results into a unified list, deduplicating by proximity or name. Apply the existing distance and availability filters to the merged list. Render each hospital using the existing HospitalCard component, passing the computed distance, parsed address, and phone. Preserve the emergency dark theme styling (charcoal background, red/amber accents) throughout.

Extend the Overpass utility to parse and export address fields (addr:housenumber, addr:street, addr:city, addr:postcode) and phone fields (phone, contact:phone) from Overpass node tags, returning them as optional string properties in the hospital result type.

requirements.summary: Display extracted address, phone, opening hours, and emergency badge in ResourceMapPage hospital popups and sidebar items
acceptanceCriteria: Popup shows hospital name, address (labeled 'Address:'), distance, phone (as a tel: link), opening hours (if available), and emergency badge (if applicable).
Sidebar list item shows hospital name, address (labeled 'Address:'), available beds (color-coded), and distance.
All popup and sidebar content uses the emergency dark theme styling (charcoal, red/amber accents).
Backend-registered hospitals fall back to their stored address and contact fields.

file_operations.description: Update the hospital marker popup content to display the hospital name, address (labeled 'Address:', extracted from Overpass addr:* tags or falling back to backend address field), distance from user, phone number as a clickable tel: link (extracted from Overpass phone/contact:phone/emergency:phone tags or backend contact field), opening hours (from Overpass opening_hours tag if available), and a '24/7 Emergency' badge if the Overpass emergency=yes or healthcare:emergency=yes tag is present. Update the sidebar list items to show hospital name, address (labeled 'Address:'), available bed count color-coded by availability level, and distance. Apply the emergency dark theme styling (charcoal background, red/amber text accents) consistently to all popup and sidebar content. For backend-registered hospitals, use the stored address and contact fields as fallback values.

requirements.summary: Completely rewrite blood type detection logic in BloodDonorPage with strict priority-ordered regex for text files and manual selector for image files
acceptanceCriteria: For text files, regex tests AB+/AB- before A+/A-, B+/B-, and O+/O- (strict priority order).
Patterns cover bare symbols, labeled formats, and spelled-out positivity/negativity.
For image files (JPG/PNG), no regex is run on binary data; a manual blood type selector is shown instead.
Manual selector must be confirmed before form submission is allowed for image uploads.
'Detected Blood Type: [X]' label appears only when detection succeeds.
If text file detection fails, an error message is shown and form submission is blocked.
Correct blood type is sent to the backend on submission.

file_operations.description: Completely rewrite the blood type detection logic. For text-based files (TXT or PDF read as text via FileReader), apply a strict priority-ordered regex that tests for AB+, AB-, A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O- in that exact order (most specific first). Patterns must match bare symbols (e.g. 'AB+'), labeled formats ('Blood Group: A+', 'Blood Type: B-', 'Group: O+'), and spelled-out forms ('A Positive', 'B Negative', 'O Positive'). For image files (JPG/PNG) where binary data cannot be parsed, do NOT run regex on raw binary or base64 content. Instead, display the inline message 'Image files cannot be analyzed automatically. Please select your blood type below.' and render a manual blood type selector dropdown (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-) that the user must select and confirm before form submission is allowed. Show 'Detected Blood Type: [X]' only when a type is positively identified from text. If detection fails on a text file, show 'Could not detect blood type from the uploaded proof. Please upload a document clearly showing your blood group.' and block form submission until a valid detection occurs or the user uploads a different file. Ensure the confirmed or detected blood type is passed to the backend addBloodDonor mutation on form submission.

Create a utility module that exports a function detectBloodTypeFromText(text: string) which applies a strict priority-ordered regex to detect blood types. Test patterns in the order AB+, AB-, A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O- (most specific first) to avoid false positives. Include patterns for bare symbols, labeled formats ('Blood Group:', 'Blood Type:', 'Group:'), and spelled-out positivity/negativity ('Positive', 'Negative'). Return the detected blood type string or null if no match is found. Add comprehensive test cases covering edge cases and priority conflicts.
